stem: For positive real α and β, evaluate lim(x→0) [(1+x)^α−1]/[(1+x)^β−1].
solution: Both numerator and denominator vanish. Their first-order expansions are αx+o(x) and βx+o(x), giving α/β.
hint: Use the derivative of a power at 1.

stem: Suppose the integer X is odd. Then X²−1 is
solution: For odd X, X²−1=(X−1)(X+1) is divisible by 8. It is either zero (X=±1) or a positive composite number. Thus it is never prime and need not be positive.
hint: Factor the difference of squares.

stem: For which k is f(x)=k exp(kx) a probability density on [0,1]?
solution: The total integral is exp(k)−1. Setting it to 1 gives exp(k)=2 and k=log 2, which also makes the density nonnegative.
hint: Normalize the density by integration.

stem: Positive integers p and q satisfy that p²−q² is prime. Then p−q is
options: An odd number greater than 1 but not prime
solution: Since (p−q)(p+q) is positive prime and p+q>p−q>0, necessarily p−q=1. None of the first three statements describes 1.
hint: Use the factorization of a difference of squares.

stem: Any non-decreasing function on [a,b]
options: Is continuous on [a,b] but not differentiable
solution: A step function is non-decreasing but discontinuous, so (A) and (B) need not hold. A constant function is non-decreasing but has no inverse.
hint: Consider a step function and a constant function.

stem: The determinant equation det[[x,3,4],[1,2,1],[1,8,1]]=0 is satisfied by
solution: Replace the third row by the third minus the second, giving [0,6,0]. Expansion along this row gives −6(x−4)=0, hence x=4.
hint: Subtract the second row from the third.

stem: If f(x)=√(x+√(x+√(x+⋯))), find f′(x) where the positive radical converges and is differentiable.
solution: The repeated tail equals f(x), so f(x)²=x+f(x). Differentiating gives (2f(x)−1)f′(x)=1.
hint: Express the infinite tail using f itself.
notes: The derivative is on the positive-input branch; the radical at the isolated endpoint x=0 needs a separate limiting convention.

stem: If P=logₓ(xy) and Q=logᵧ(xy), then P+Q equals
solution: Write a=log x and b=log y. Then P=(a+b)/a and Q=(a+b)/b, so P+Q=(a+b)²/(ab)=PQ.
hint: Change both logarithms to the same base.
notes: Assume the displayed logarithms exist: x,y>0 and x,y≠1.

stem: Evaluate ∫(2x³+1)/(x⁴+2x) dx.
solution: The derivative of the denominator is 4x³+2, twice the numerator. Substitution u=x⁴+2x yields (1/2)∫du/u.
hint: Compare the numerator with the denominator’s derivative.

stem: Find all x for which x²−3x+2>0.
solution: Factor (x−1)(x−2). The product is positive outside the two roots, excluding both roots.
hint: Use a sign chart.

stem: On the real line let f₁(x)=x² and f₂(x)=4x³+7. Which statement is correct?
options: f₁ is one-to-one and onto but f₂ is not
f₂ is one-to-one and onto but f₁ is not
answer: f₂ is one-to-one and onto but f₁ is not
solution: The cubic is strictly increasing and has range ℝ. The square takes the same value at x and −x and never takes negative values.
hint: Check injectivity and the full real range.

stem: If f(x)=((a+x)/(b+x))^(a+b+2x), with a,b>0, find f′(0).
solution: Logarithmic differentiation gives f′/f=2 log((a+x)/(b+x))+(a+b+2x)[1/(a+x)−1/(b+x)]. At zero the bracketed second contribution is (a+b)(b−a)/(ab)=(b²−a²)/(ab), and f(0)=(a/b)^(a+b).
hint: Take logarithms before differentiating.

stem: Maximize z=0.5x+1.5y subject to x+y≤6, 3x+y≤15, x+3y≤15, x,y≥0. The problem has
solution: The objective is 0.5(x+3y), so it cannot exceed 7.5. Every point on the feasible segment from (0,5) to (1.5,4.5) attains 7.5; hence infinitely many optima exist.
hint: Compare the objective with the third constraint.

stem: For 0<θ<1, let f(x;θ)=θf(x;1)+(1−θ)f(x;0), where f(x;1) and f(x;0) are probability densities. Then
options: f(x;θ) is a density for all allowed θ
It is a density only for 0<θ<1/2
It is a density only for 1/2≤θ<1
answer: f(x;θ) is a density for all allowed θ
solution: A convex combination of nonnegative functions is nonnegative. Its integral is θ+(1−θ)=1 for every allowed θ.
hint: Check nonnegativity and total integral.

stem: For observations (x,y)=(5,0),(1,4),(4,2),(3,0),(2,−1), the correlation r satisfies
solution: The means are x̄=3 and ȳ=1. The centered cross-product sum is −5; the centered square sums are 10 and 16. Thus r=−5/√160≈−0.395, between −0.5 and zero.
hint: Compute centered cross products.

stem: A function is homothetic if it is an increasing transformation of a degree-one homogeneous function. For xᵢ>0, 0<r<1 and aᵢ>0, let f₁=Σxᵢʳ and f₂=Σaᵢxᵢ+b. Then
solution: The function g₁=(Σxᵢʳ)^(1/r) is homogeneous of degree one, and f₁=g₁ʳ is an increasing transformation. Also g₂=Σaᵢxᵢ is homogeneous of degree one, and f₂=g₂+b is an increasing transformation.
hint: Apply the power 1/r to the first function.

stem: If h(x)=1/(1−x), find h(h(h(x))).
solution: The second iterate is (x−1)/x. Applying h again gives 1/[1−(x−1)/x]=x. The composition requires x≠0,1.
hint: Calculate the second iterate first.

stem: The function x|x|+(|x|/x)³ is
options: Continuous but not differentiable at x=0
solution: For x>0 the function is x²+1, whose right limit is 1. For x<0 it is −x²−1, whose left limit is −1. No value assigned at zero can make it continuous.
hint: Evaluate the two one-sided limits.
notes: The printed formula is undefined at zero; it has no continuous extension there.

stem: Evaluate ∫2/[(x−2)(x−1)x] dx.
solution: Partial fractions give 1/x−2/(x−1)+1/(x−2). Integrating and combining logarithms gives log|x(x−2)/(x−1)²|+C.
hint: Use partial fractions at the three simple poles.

stem: Each restaurant reservation independently has a 20% chance of not showing up. There are 50 tables and 52 reservations. What is the probability of accommodating everyone?
solution: If N is the number showing up, N~Binomial(52,0.8). Failure occurs only when 51 or 52 show. Its probability is 52(0.8)^51(0.2)+(0.8)^52=14(0.8)^52. Subtract from 1.
hint: Only two possible attendance counts exceed capacity.
notes: The source does not explicitly state independence; the standard binomial model is used.

stem: With [x]=floor(x), evaluate I=∫₀^(3/2) {[x]+[x²]} dx.
solution: On [0,1), both floors vanish. On [1,√2), their sum is 2; on [√2,3/2], their sum is 3. Thus I=2(√2−1)+3(3/2−√2)=5/2−√2.
hint: Split at the integer thresholds of x and x².

stem: Every integer of the form (n³−n)(n²−4), n=3,4,…, is
solution: The expression is (n−2)(n−1)n(n+1)(n+2), the product of five consecutive integers. It equals 5! times an integer, hence is divisible by 120. At n=3 it equals 120, which is not divisible by 720.
hint: Factor into five consecutive integers.

stem: Mango varieties A and B cost p₁ and p₂ rupees per kg. Buyer 1 buys 5 kg A and 10 kg B; buyer 2 spends Rs 100 on A and Rs 150 on B. If their average expenditure per mango (irrespective of variety) is the same, which statement is most appropriate?
answer: Intended: C, p₁=p₂ or p₂=3p₁/4; literal wording lacks unit-weight information.
solution: If “per mango” means per kg, equality gives (5p₁+10p₂)/15=250/(100/p₁+150/p₂). Simplifying yields (p₁−p₂)(3p₁−4p₂)=0, so option C. Literally per mango requires the number or average weight of mangoes of each variety, which is not provided.
hint: Write each buyer’s total spending divided by total quantity.
notes: Source mixes prices per kg with an average per mango; intended answer requires equal average mango weights or replacing “per mango” with “per kg”.

stem: For paired data, the squared correlation coefficient between x² and y is 1. Which statement follows about the (x,y) scatter diagram?
options: All points lie on a straight line
All points lie on y=a+bx² with a>0,b>0
All points lie on y=a+bx² for real a,b
answer: All points lie on y=a+bx² for real a,b
solution: Absolute correlation one means an exact affine relation between y and the transformed variable x²: y=a+bx², with nonzero b when correlation is defined. Neither intercept nor slope has a required positive sign.
hint: Treat x² as a new variable.

stem: How many permutations of 1,…,7 have both 1 and 2 before 3 and both 6 and 7 after 3?
solution: Among the 5! relative orders of {1,2,3,6,7}, exactly 2!·2!=4 satisfy the restrictions. Each relative order occurs equally often in the 7! full permutations, so the count is 7!·4/5!=168.
hint: First count the allowed relative orders of five constrained entries.

stem: A continuous real function on [0,∞) satisfies f(x)=xf(x). What is f(2)?
solution: For every x≠1, (1−x)f(x)=0 forces f(x)=0. Continuity then forces f(1)=0 too. Consequently f(2)=0=f(1).
hint: Rearrange the functional equation, then use continuity at 1.

stem: A variable X takes 0,1,…,n with probabilities proportional to C(n,0),C(n,1),…,C(n,n). Find mean μ and variance σ².
solution: The binomial coefficients sum to 2ⁿ, so P(X=k)=C(n,k)(1/2)ⁿ. This is Binomial(n,1/2), with mean n/2 and variance n/4.
hint: Identify the normalized binomial distribution.

stem: Five points are placed anywhere inside a square of side 2. Which statement is incorrect?
options: No two points have distance greater than 2√2
Partition into four unit squares: some unit square has at least two points on or inside it
At least two points have distance less than √2
Statements A, B and C are all incorrect
answer: Intended D for strict interior points; C and D are false if the boundary is included.
solution: A follows from the square’s diameter and B from the pigeonhole principle. If “inside” means strict interior, C is true: two points in a common half-square cannot be opposite external corners, hence a pair has distance strictly below √2, making D the sole false statement. If boundary points are allowed, the four vertices and center have minimum distance √2, so C is false as well as D.
hint: Partition the square into four equal squares and check strict versus weak inequalities.
notes: Strict “less than” creates a boundary-convention ambiguity. Four vertices plus the center are a counterexample if boundary points are allowed.

stem: A differentiable real function satisfies f(x)f′(x)<0 for all real x. Then
solution: The condition ensures f never vanishes. Thus |f| is differentiable with derivative f f′/|f|<0. The sign of f itself may be positive or negative, so its direction of change alone is not determined.
hint: Differentiate |f| using that f never equals zero.

stem: For positive p,q,r,s, (p²+p+1)(q²+q+1)(r²+r+1)(s²+s+1)/(pqrs) is at least
solution: Each factor after division by its variable is t+1+1/t≥3 by t+1/t≥2. Multiplying four such bounds gives 3⁴=81, attained at p=q=r=s=1.
hint: Apply AM–GM to t and 1/t.
